title: Why Do Rolls-Royce Wheel Logos Never Spin?
description:
Watch the wheels of a Rolls-Royce as it drives away. The wheels spin, but the R R logo in the middle stays perfectly upright, as if it were painted on the air. It is not magic, and it is not a camera trick. Today, ten parts of a Rolls-Royce that look like luxury tricks, and the engineering reason behind each one.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:01 1. The floating wheel logo
2:03 2. The umbrella in the door
3:03 3. The hiding mascot
4:08 4. The coach doors
5:17 5. The starlight headliner
6:20 6. The camera that reads the road
7:18 7. The power reserve gauge
8:29 8. The Pantheon grille
9:30 9. The painted coachline
10:31 10. The silent cabin
11:38 The verdict

Sources:
- Rolls-Royce self-righting wheel centres, umbrella in the door, coach doors, Starlight headliner: Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Press Club https://www.press.rolls-roycemotorcars.com/
- Spirit of Ecstasy, Charles Sykes 1911, retractable mechanism: Wikipedia, "Spirit of Ecstasy" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_of_Ecstasy
- Rolls-Royce Phantom VIII, Flagbearer camera, magic carpet ride, 6.75-litre V12, sound insulation: Wikipedia, "Rolls-Royce Phantom (2017)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Phantom_VIII
- Red Flag Act (Locomotive Act 1865): Wikipedia, "Locomotive Acts" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locomotive_Acts
- Ghost (2020) tuned cabin sound: Wikipedia, "Rolls-Royce Ghost" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Ghost
- Rolls-Royce Spectre: Wikipedia, "Rolls-Royce Spectre" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Spectre
